hero.title: Sidewalks, street trees and **wet ground.**
hero.lede: Grand Scapes looks after Swartz Creek yards: weekly mowing, fall leaf cleanup, bed makeovers and driveway plowing. Most homes here went up between the 1950s and the 1970s, on streets with sidewalks and trees, and the ground near the creek stays wet.

about.title: A 1950s city built **beside a floodplain.**
body: Swartz Creek grew up as a home for industrial workers and their families. The city's master plan says most of its single family homes were built in the 1950s and 60s, concentrated on the west side in and around Winchester Village, which the plan calls one of the first uniform housing developments finished with sewer, water, paved streets, sidewalks and street trees. More than a thousand of the city's homes date from the 1950s through the 1970s.

The creek runs right through town and, in the plan's words, serves primarily as a drain, with a watershed that lies mostly south of the city and empties into the Flint River. Because so much of the city sits along its floodplain, the plan describes the water table as moderate to high, with poor drainage and wet soil. That shows up as soggy back corners, soft lawns after a storm and beds that never quite dry.

Newer homes fill in the edges: Heritage Village east of downtown, a planned community with alleys and common areas, the growing Miller neighborhood, and the wooded, low density lots of Markwood. Each asks something a little different of a lawn crew.

points.title: A sidewalk with a deadline
points.body: The city's sidewalk ordinance puts the walk out front on the occupant and allows 48 hours after snow or ice falls to clear it, the full width on walks up to 60 inches. If it is left, the city can clear it and charge the property. People who leave for the winter are told to arrange it ahead.

points.title: No cars on the street overnight
points.body: The city's fall newsletter reminds residents that there is no parking on any city street from 2 to 6 AM. More cars sit in driveways overnight, and that shapes how a drive gets plowed.

points.title: Small lots on soft ground
points.body: The plan says most lots in neighborhoods like Park, Elms and Atkins Acres are small, and the soil across the city tends to stay wet. Heavy mowers rut a soggy lawn, so timing matters more than horsepower.

points.title: Leaves go out in paper
points.body: Yard waste goes out with the trash on Tuesdays from April through November, in paper yard waste bags or a marked container of 30 pounds or less, never plastic. The city also asks that leaves never go into storm drains or ditches, which run straight to the river.

points.title: Street trees and old foundation beds
points.body: Most local streets have trees along the right of way, and a house from the 1950s or 60s can carry foundation shrubs that outgrew their spot long ago. Those older front beds are where a makeover changes the most.

logistics.title: Getting a Swartz Creek yard on the schedule.
body: Rob answers the phone and the texts. Tell him the address and what you want handled, and he will come out, walk the yard with you, point out what it needs and give you a price. Mowing and plowing go on a regular route; cleanups and bed work get a date.

Swartz Creek is about 25 minutes west of our shop on Embury Road in Grand Blanc. On a city lot the trailer usually parks at the curb, so mention a narrow drive, a busy street or a dog in the yard at that first visit.
Call [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040), [text Rob](sms:+18109903040) or send the [estimate form](/get-an-estimate/).

faq.q: Do you do lawn care in Swartz Creek, MI?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes works in Swartz Creek from our shop in Grand Blanc. We do [weekly lawn mowing](/lawn-mowing-swartz-creek-mi/), [fall leaf removal](/leaf-removal-swartz-creek-mi/), [mulch and bed work](/mulch-installation-swartz-creek-mi/), [landscaping](/landscaping-swartz-creek-mi/) and [snow removal](/snow-removal-swartz-creek-mi/) here, plus [spring cleanups](/spring-cleanup/). Overgrown bushes and small trees, yes; big trees, no.

faq.q: How long do I have to clear my sidewalk in Swartz Creek?
faq.a: The city's sidewalk ordinance, Section 15-21, says snow and ice must be cleared no later than 48 hours after it fell or accumulated, and walks up to 60 inches wide are cleared the full width. If it is not done, the city can have it cleared and the cost becomes a lien on the property. Check the city's notice for the current wording.

faq.q: Does Swartz Creek pick up leaves?
faq.a: Leaves go out with yard waste on Tuesdays, April through November, in paper yard waste bags or a marked container that weighs 30 pounds or less, according to the city calendar. Plastic bags are not accepted. A [fall cleanup](/leaf-removal-swartz-creek-mi/) skips the bags: we vacuum the leaves into our trailer and haul them off.

faq.q: Who plows the streets in Swartz Creek?
faq.a: Inside the city, the Department of Public Services plows city streets, and the city asks that driveway snow not be pushed into the road. County roads in the townships around the city belong to the Genesee County Road Commission, which plows subdivision streets last. Your driveway and walk are yours, and that is what we clear.

faq.q: How tall can grass get before the city calls it a violation?
faq.a: The city's weed and grass ordinance, Section 20-21 on the city calendar, says grass and other rank growth may not be taller than six inches on average. A wet week in June and a vacation can get you close. Weekly [mowing](/lawn-mowing-swartz-creek-mi/) keeps it well under.
